$about: The Labs page (examples/labs.html, my-3d2dge.vercel.app/labs) is built from this list by tools/build.mjs, in the list's order. check (To check) holds what only the owner can judge (feel, sound, a real phone): each entry says what to do (what) and what to look for (look), its title opening the place (at: what to add to the address); it goes once checked. Each section has a title (short: a shorter name for the bar at the top, if it needs one), a line saying what it holds (about) and its entries; line: true numbers them, one line in the order it was made, each with made (when it was made). Each entry is one page: page is an examples/ page name (examples/<page>.html, served at /<page>) or a dist/ path; its title opens the page, and links are other places to start, [label, what to add to the address] (or another dist/ path). line, kits and keep (Tools) are kept. temporary holds the prototypes (DOCTRINE.md) in the order they were made, one-off comparisons and experiments, each with the date it was added and the question it answers; next: the page it led to, and deviates: one line for each way it departs from the doctrine, if any. When the question is settled, delete the page and its entry, or graduate it to another section (it is then held to the engine tier). A change to a prototype alone needs no version bump. tools/labs-test.mjs opens every link.

sections.title: To check
sections.about: What only a person can judge: how it feels in the hands, how it sounds, how it plays on a real phone. Each card says what to do and what to look for, and its button opens the place. Tell Claude what you find (a line is enough); a card goes once it is checked.

entries.title: Roguelike on your phone
entries.what: Open it on your phone and play a floor or two: tap a cell to walk there, hold the stick to step, WAIT, POTION and SCROLL at the side. Added with v0.63.0 (Milestone 2).
entries.look: Does a tap walk where you meant? Are the buttons in reach of a thumb? Can you read the crypt in the dark (the torchlight, the fog over what you saw before)? Does a run feel fair: bats twice your speed, slimes half?

entries.title: Puzzle: how the blocks handle
entries.what: Play BLOCKS for a few minutes with the keys (arrows, Space drop, C hold), then on your phone (drag, tap, flick down, flick up); then a round of PAIRS. Added with v0.63.0 (Milestone 2).
entries.look: Does it handle like a modern Tetris: the auto-shift when you hold a side, the turn by a wall (kicks), time to slide a piece once it lands? On the phone, does a flick drop or hold every time, and never by mistake? In PAIRS, does a chain feel worth it?

entries.title: Arcade: do the three classics feel right?
entries.what: Play each cabinet for a few minutes, on the keys or a pad (arrows, Space fires; in ROCKS up thrusts, X warps), then once on your phone. Press C (a pad's Y) in a game to switch to the classic look and back. Lose all your lives once to see the continue, the letter wheel and the table; leave the cabinet alone for 20 seconds to see the demo. Added with v0.64.0 (Milestone 3).
entries.look: MAZE: does a turn pressed early happen at the next corner, and do the four wisps feel different (one chases, one cuts you off, one flanks, one is shy)? FORMATION: do the dives look like Galaga's swoops, and is it fair? ROCKS: do thrust and drift feel weighty, and do the glowing lines read well? Is the remaster or the classic look better, and are the cabinet's sides too busy?

entries.title: Shooter: the horizontal stage
entries.what: Play stage 2 to its end: pick up the red capsules and press X (or POWER on a phone) to take the lit power on the bar at the bottom; get a couple of OPTIONs and watch them trail you; beat the cruiser and the core behind its walls. Then play the vertical stage from the start to see it lead into stage 2. Added with v0.64.0 (Milestone 3).
entries.look: Does it feel like Gradius: the power bar's choices, the options following your path, the rock you must not touch? Is it too hard or too easy (the core, the cavern's guns)? Is the cavern readable on your phone, with the bar above the touch area?

sections.title: The road to Emberdeep
sections.about: One line, in the order it was made: each of these grew the engine, and together they led to the showcase game.

entries.title: Scarfrunner
entries.what: The side-scrolling prototype: platforming, a physics scarf and parallax.

entries.title: Emberwell
entries.what: The action-RPG arena demo with GPU lighting. It opens isometric; three more views below.

entries.title: Perspective Lab
entries.what: One room in every camera view (isometric, three-quarter, top-down, brawler, side), with skeleton and lighting toggles.

entries.title: Stress test
entries.what: Raise the load (up to 5,000 monsters, torches, particles) until the frame rate drops, or run the benchmark to rate this device. Any view the engine can draw (side scrolling, with depth drawn the Mode 7 way, or a custom turn and tilt), fixed in place if you like.

entries.title: Emberdeep
entries.what: The showcase game. Its own test areas are inside it: the Proving Grounds, the Gallery (every monster, skill and pose) and Settings' Tools (spawn any monster, jump to any depth, make any item).

sections.title: Starter kits
sections.about: Small games for an AI model to build from: one genre each, engine and API card included. The 3D ones put a real 3D world (three.js and Rapier) under the game.

entries.title: Adventure
entries.what: Top-down action adventure (Secret of Mana, Zelda): a village, ruins and a shrine.

entries.title: Platformer
entries.what: Side-scroller (Castlevania, Mega Man X): a night approach to a castle, in five zones.

entries.title: Brawler
entries.what: Beat-'em-up (Final Fight, Streets of Rage 2): a city block at dusk, wave after wave.

entries.title: Shooter
entries.what: Vertical shoot-'em-up (Raiden, 1943): farmland, a river town and an air base; then a horizontal stage (Gradius, R-Type): a crystal cavern, a power bar, options, a cruiser and a core battleship. A continue, initials and a table.

entries.title: Arcade
entries.what: A cabinet of three (Pac-Man, Galaga, Asteroids): a maze with four chasers, moths that fly in and dive, rocks that split and wrap; high-score tables with initials, two players taking turns, a demo when left alone; each a remaster with its classic look one key away.

entries.title: RPG battle
entries.what: Side-view battle (Final Fantasy VI, Chrono Trigger): three heroes, three monsters.

entries.title: Roguelike
entries.what: Turn-based crypt (Rogue, Mystery Dungeon): ten generated floors, fog, bats that move twice, the Amulet at the bottom.

entries.title: Puzzle
entries.what: Falling blocks by today's rules (Tetris) and falling pairs that chain (Puyo Puyo), with a mascot.

entries.title: Stealth
entries.what: Rooftops at dusk (Tenchu, Assassin's Creed): steal the ledger past three guards.

entries.title: Animation lab
entries.what: Every move, pose and skin the character rigs have, from every view.

entries.title: All in one file
entries.what: The engine, its API card, all eight games and the animation lab, with a title menu. A kit is one game of it, small enough for a chat model.

entries.title: 3D action
entries.what: A torch-lit hall in real 3D (Zelda 64, Diablo): a combo, a dash, a jump and a bolt against five waves, then a knight.

entries.title: 3D platformer
entries.what: A sunlit course of islands over the void (Mario 64, Spyro): double jumps, moving platforms, springs, coins and three stars.

entries.title: 3D shooter
entries.what: An open world two kilometres across (Apex Legends without the multiplayer), first or third person: sprint, slide, vault, mantle, climb, ziplines, kick doors in; a rifle, a shotgun, a punch and grenades against raiders holding five outposts.

entries.title: 3D in one file
entries.what: The 3D engine (three.js r182 and Rapier, under the 2D engine), its manual, the API card and all three 3D games. Served, not opened from a disk.

sections.title: Tools
sections.about: For looking closely: every imported animation clip, on a mannequin and on the hero.

entries.title: Mocap Lab
entries.what: Every imported animation clip, on a mannequin and on the hero, in every view, slow or frame by frame. Sets: Quaternius, Mesh2Motion, CMU motion capture, and the clips the hero uses; the CMU library holds every one of its 2,548 takes.

entries.title: Asset Lab
entries.what: Every object, material and sprite a game can use without drawing code: the engine's core library and the asset store's sets (Kenney and KayKit models, ambientCG materials, Kenney pixel packs, all CC0), searchable, in every view and turning beside the hero, each with its text to copy or edit and where it came from.

sections.title: Temporary
sections.about: Prototypes, each answering one question, in the order they were made. Once a question is answered, its page is deleted or kept as a tool.
sections.empty: Nothing here right now. One-off comparisons and experiments land here, each with its date and the question it answers.
